inspiration.note: Idea only: one idea, an LLM shot planner, short clips joined into one film. No media from the post is used; this graph uses Seedance 1.5 Pro clips and nanoodle's Combine node.

results.label: Shot planner
results.text:
HERO: A tiny hand-folded bright yellow paper boat, small as a child's palm, crisp folded creases, slightly dampened at the bow.

STYLE: 35mm film look with soft grain, deep night blues and purples cut by neon pinks and oranges warming to golden sunrise, shallow depth of field, anamorphic lens flares, wet reflective surfaces.

SHOT 1: Extreme close-up at gutter level, a child's hand lowers the yellow paper boat into a rushing rain-filled gutter beside a curb; camera slowly pushes in as fingers release and the current catches the boat, neon signs reflecting in the dark water around it.

SHOT 2: Low tracking shot gliding alongside the boat at water level as it races down the gutter channel, camera moving parallel in a steady lateral dolly; rain streaks fall and the boat bobs and tilts through splashes, weaving past glowing pink and cyan reflections stretching across the wet asphalt.

SHOT 3: Wide shot from behind and slightly above as the gutter empties into a calm harbor; camera cranes up slowly as the yellow paper boat drifts out onto still water, the rising sun painting the sky gold, its small silhouette growing peaceful against the vast glowing horizon.

verdicts.Shot 1: A hand lowers the yellow paper boat into a narrow wet gutter; it settles and floats with pink neon reflections around it.
verdicts.Shot 2: Opens on two hands shaping and setting the boat on dark water, repeating the launch beat, then the boat drifts along the wet gutter past pink and teal reflections.
verdicts.Shot 3: The boat sits at the mouth of a stone channel over dark water, then floats out across a calm harbor at sunrise, small against the horizon with moored boats on the skyline.
verdicts.Film: 15.1 s, 1280x720, 24 fps, silent. The same folded yellow boat appears in all three shots. Cuts are hard cuts with no transitions; shot 2 restarts the launch instead of continuing it.

graphNote: as-run-graph.json is the exact file the run used. Its Combine links target clip1, clip2 and clip3. graph.json and workflow.json are the same graph with those three ports renamed to vid1, vid2 and vid3, the port names the editor's Combine node uses. nanoodle-js accepts both names and orders them by number (src/nodes.mjs combine), so the run is the same. workflow.json also moves nodes so they don't overlap in the editor.
